content: At present, there are no medications approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) specifically for the treatment of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH). For patients who have both type 2 diabetes and NASH, the primary focus of treatment is on achieving optimal glucose control and implementing strategies for effective weight management. Pioglitazone, a thiazolidinedione, has demonstrated efficacy in improving steatohepatitis and reducing liver fibrosis. Certain GLP-1 receptor agonists have also been shown to be effective in managing steatohepatitis and decreasing the progression of liver fibrosis. In patients with significant liver fibrosis, defined as fibrosis stage F2 or greater, these agents are recommended as part of the therapeutic approach.
